newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta starts weak, braked by intervention fears.
newsitem.headline: Peseta starts weak, braked by intervention fears.

text.p: Spain's peseta opened weaker versus the mark, though the fall was braked by fears of possible intervention by the Bank of Spain.

"On Friday the Bank of Spain had to intervene massively to defend the peseta...up to now we haven't seen the central bank, and it seems it is the market maintaining this level," a dealer in Madrid said.
However other dealers did not rule out further weakening later today forcing the Bank of Spain to buy pesetas.
Last Friday the Bank of Spain sanctioned its second official rate cut in the year, cutting 25 basis points to 5.75 percent.
The peseta's weakness was seen as a part of an European movement, where lira and escudo were weak as well, due to EMU's jitters.
Around 0920 GMT, the peseta was trading around 84.92/95 per mark versus an opening level around 84.94/96 and closing level on Friday at 84.92/95.
